title: 2017 MAZDA MX-5 Miata

highlights: Low mileage (24,800 mi) with single-owner history
6-speed manual, desirable Soul Red Metallic color
New tires and battery per seller
red_flags: Vehicle history report indicates accident or damage reported, contradicting seller's claim of flawless, pristine condition
normalized.prelim_summary: This 2017 Mazda MX-5 Miata Sport is a low-mileage, manual-transmission convertible in an attractive Soul Red Metallic finish, offered by a private seller in Napa, CA for $20,500. While the seller describes it as meticulously maintained with new tires and battery, the vehicle history report notes an accident or damage, which buyers should investigate further before purchase.

contradictions.detail: The description calls the car 'flawless', 'pristine' and in 'showroom condition' and says it 'needs absolutely nothing'. It does not mention the two bumper damage events AutoCheck reports (12/2020 and 09/2021). The listing page's own history badge does show 'Accident or Damage Reported'.
The seller description states an asking price of $19,500, while the listing price is $20,500. The tracker shows a raise from $19,500 to $20,500 on 2026-10-19.

critical_evidence.evidence: AutoCheck shows dealer 'recommended maintenance' entries in 2019 and 11/2024 but no itemised oil-change dates and no brake-fluid flush. There is no reported entry for about 5 years (07/2019–11/2024). The 'freshly serviced' claim has no receipt.

There are no transmission repair or warranty records and no door-jamb photo examined here. AutoCheck puts manufacture at 08/2017, which is late MY2017 production and outside the highest-risk early-ND1 window, but the gearbox is not documented.
No photos with the carpet lifted or of the drain area behind the seats were examined here. The visible floor mats look dry and only lightly dusty.

AutoCheck reports 'No Open Recalls' and recall service performed 06/2019, 07/2019 and 11/21/2024. The 11/2024 visit likely covers airbag campaign 24V695000. TCM recall 19V072000 does not apply to this manual car.

The engine-bay photo shows a Super Start battery with a '12/25' date sticker, which supports a recent battery. The tires look near-new but the DOT code is not legible, and there are no receipts for the tires or the 'fresh service'.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is solid: a VIN, a clean-title AutoCheck with one owner, a consistent odometer, a passed 2025 smog and recalls closed. The maintenance half is incomplete: dealer entries exist but are not itemised, there is a 5-year reporting gap, there is no brake-fluid record, and the two bumper events have no repair invoices.

condition.rationale: The photos show a clean engine bay, a dated recent battery, near-new tires, a good-looking soft top and a tidy interior. Against that are two reported bumper damage events and an apparent scuff on the rear bumper corner in the rear three-quarter photo. The underside, cabin water areas and gearbox are unexamined.

price_value.rationale: $20,500 is just under the low end of the $20,919–$23,747 fair-value estimate. That estimate leans on pricier trims, and the profile band for a 2017 Sport at about 25k mi is $17–20k. Two minor accident reports further weaken resale, so this is roughly fair rather than a bargain.

mission_fit.rationale: This is a manual, reliable, low-mileage ND roadster within the max-price band and suited to coastal driving with easy resale. It is held back by the price sitting slightly above the ideal band, the accident history, and the possibility it has already sold.

logistics.rationale: Napa, CA is a straightforward drive from Carmel. The car has CA registration and passed smog in 2025, and a local PPI is feasible. PPI access is not stated, and the tracker shows the same VIN marked sold on 2026-10-23.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: It has a desirable Soul Red paint and a 6-speed manual, appears stock, and has had one owner. It is the base Sport trim with a budget replacement tire and no Club or Brembo/BBS content.

ppi_focus: Paint-depth readings on both bumpers, the quarters and the aluminum front fenders, and panel gaps, to assess the two bumper repairs.
Bumper mounts, crash bars and headlight and taillight brackets for hidden collision damage.
Gearbox: warm shifts into 2nd and 3rd for grinding, plus clutch engagement point and slip in 5th and 6th.
Soft-top drains, footwell underlay moisture, and seat-rail bolt corrosion.
Soft-top rear-corner and header wear, and a seal leak test.
Underside: diff pinion and output seals, valve cover, front crank seal, and the water pump weep hole.
Brake-fluid moisture test, and a scan for stored codes.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: repair invoices showing the bumper events were cosmetic and repaired properly, plus a clean PPI with matching paint readings.
Up: itemised service invoices including a brake-fluid flush and tire receipts with recent DOT dates.
Up: price movement toward $18–19k to reflect the accident history.
Down: confirmation the car has sold, a refused PPI, evidence of structural or poorly repaired damage, cabin water, or warm-gear grinding.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, reliable ND roadster close to Carmel fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and should resell easily within 6–24 months. The undisclosed accident history and possible sale are the open issues.
evidence.rationale: AutoCheck establishes the identity and history well: a clean title, one owner since 10/2017, a consistent odometer (23,685 at 11/2025, 24,800 now), a passed 2025 smog, and no open recalls with recall work logged 11/2024. It also records two minor collisions with bumper damage, in 12/2020 and 09/2021. The seller's 'flawless, showroom, needs absolutely nothing' description does not disclose them, and no repair documentation is offered. The photos show a clean stock engine bay, a battery dated 12/25, near-new Sailun tires with unreadable date codes, and an apparent scuff on the rear bumper corner. Maintenance evidence consists of non-itemised dealer entries with a roughly 5-year reporting gap and no brake-fluid record, so time-based service is unproven. The 08/2017 build date places the gearbox outside the main early-ND1 risk window, but there are no transmission records. The $20,500 asking price sits near the lower edge of the fair-value estimate and above the profile's Sport band. The tracker shows this VIN marked sold on 2026-10-23.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller to confirm the car is still available. If it is, request the bumper repair invoices, itemised service records, tire DOT photos and permission for a PPI near Napa.
